Theneed to open markets is becoming increasingly apparent to developingnations, and leaders have sought to convince their people and industries of thisneed. As one economist noted, deregulating the economy may be the only wayto dismantle the monopolies and oligopolies controlled by families andcronies. Emerging economies, however, face a dilemma. While they are soeager to attract foreign investment and technology transfer in order to becomemore globally competitive, they are obligated to protect their infant industries.One of the red flags that leaders must keep it in mind that economic growth isnot an objective itself. Rather, the goal is to ensure the reciprocal impact ofeconomic developments on enhancing the quality of life of their own people.Essay Question: Based on the short passage, write a brief critical responsesharing your perspective. In this essay, you should clearly state yourstance, analyze critically and support your view with concrete example(s)or logical reasoning. Do not repeat what is in the passage. (350-400 words )

請將下列中文短文翻譯成英文。（20 分）日益加劇的社會與政治兩極化，對民主體制造成極大壓力；極端主義的社會、文化及政治運動，也不斷挑戰制度的韌性與大眾的信任。不平等被視為是環環相扣的全球危機之一。民怨與根深蒂固的權力之間的越發衝突，反映出人們對傳統治理體制的失望，令許多人有強力疏離感，並且越來越懷疑政策制定是否能為生活帶來實質的改善。雪上加霜的是，錯誤和虛假新聞已成為另一個嚴重的全球問題。在事實被操弄與被捏造的情況下，完整的民主參與也面臨巨大挑戰。

請將下列英文短文翻譯成中文。（20 分）There are two types of arguments reverberate through debates about whatmoney should and should not buy. Consider organ trade. Those who say noargue that such markets prey upon the needy, whose choice to sell their organsoccurs under financial duress. Or others may argue that such marketsnormalize an ethically flawed view of organs as commodities, rendering thehuman person as a collection of spare parts. Meanwhile, it is worth clarifyingthese two arguments for the moral limits of markets. The first objection pointsto the injustice that can arise when people buy and sell things under conditionsof inequality or dire economic necessity; hence a person’s agreement may notreally be voluntary. They may be unfairly coerced by their situation. The otherobjection points to the degrading effect of market valuation. According to thisobjection, certain moral and civic values are diminished or corrupted if boughtand sold. Putting a price tag on human organs undermines the sanctity ofhuman life. Organ sales will remain ethically controversial.

mcq.q: What is the main argument of the passage?
opts: The most effective way to read quickly is to eliminate subvocalization and eye movement.
Neuroscience supports speed reading as a valuable tool for increasing reading performance.
Speed reading techniques can significantly improve reading efficiency without affecting comprehension.
Speed reading claims are largely unsupported by scientific research, as comprehension decreases withincreased speed.
mcq.passage: The concept of speed reading has long been promoted as a method to dramatically increase reading speed while maintaining comprehension. Numerous programs and apps claim to help individuals read at rates far beyond the average 200–400 words per minute without sacrificing understanding. However, neuroscientific research suggests otherwise. While speed reading techniques may allow for faster word recognition, they come at the cost of comprehension and retention. One of the most common speed reading techniques involves reducing subvocalization, or the internal voice that naturally accompanies reading. While limiting this may slightly increase speed, it also impairs comprehension, as language processing heavily relies on phonological (sound-based) encoding. Simply put, understanding text without subvocalization is extremely difficult because the brain processes written words in a way that is inherently linked to spoken language. Despite bold claims, research consistently discredits speed reading courses. One famous study involved two individuals who claimed to read at over 100,000 words per minute. When tested in a laboratory setting, they were able to scan pages at lightning speed, but their comprehension scores were almost non-existent. The only skill they demonstrated was an impressive ability to turn pages quickly. Another approach commonly found in speed reading apps is Rapid Serial Visual Presentation, in which words appear one at a time in a fixed position. This method eliminates eye movement, which proponents claim is unnecessary. However, as reading speed increases, comprehension drops sharply. Studies indicate that readers struggle to process meaning when words are flashed too quickly, reinforcing the idea that natural reading processes cannot be bypassed. Neuroscience debunks speed reading as an effective tool for comprehension. While individuals may train themselves to read slightly faster, true mastery of reading comes from consistent practice, enhanced vocabulary, and focused engagement. Just as musicians or athletes refine their craft through years of practice, reading is a skill that must be developed over time. The reality is clear: there are no shortcuts to deep comprehension.
